relations.subject: Soyen Shaku
relations.evidence: Soyen was a disciple of Imakita Kosen.

relations.subject: Soyen Shaku
relations.evidence: He studied for three years at Keio University.

relations.subject: Soyen Shaku
relations.evidence: Upon his return to Japan in 1890, he taught at the Nagata Zendo.

relations.subject: Soyen Shaku
relations.evidence: In 1892, upon Kosen's death, Shaku became Zen master of Engaku-ji.

relations.subject: Soyen Shaku
relations.evidence: From 1914 to 1917, Shaku served as the president of the Rinzai sect university, Rinzaishū Daigaku (today Hanazono University) in Kyoto.

relations.subject: D. T. Suzuki
relations.evidence: He had prepared a speech in Japan, and had it translated into English by his (then young and unknown) student D. T. Suzuki.

relations.subject: D. T. Suzuki
relations.evidence: Shaku, upon returning to Japan asked his student and Tokyo University scholar D. T. Suzuki to go to the United States

relations.subject: Nyogen Senzaki
relations.evidence: Shortly after arriving, Shaku was joined by his student Nyogen Senzaki.
